source_text: Ὅτι οὐ δεῖ ἱερατικοὺς ἀπὸ πρεσβυτέρων ἕως διακόνων, καὶ ἑξῆς τῆς ἐκκλησιαστικῆς τάξεως ἕως ὑπηρετῶν, ἢ ἀναγνωστῶν, ἢ ψαλτῶν, ἢ ἐφορκιστῶν, ἢ θυρωρῶν, ἢ τοῦ τάγματος τῶν ἀσκητῶν, εἰς καπηλεῖον εἰσιέναι.
thought_title: Clergy and church orders barred from taverns
orientation: The council is issuing a series of disciplinary canons; this one forbids all ranks of clergy and church orders from entering a tavern.
pass_a_gloss: That it is not necessary for sacred persons from presbyters as far as deacons, and in order of the ecclesiastical rank as far as servants, or readers, or singers, or exorcists, or doorkeepers, or of the order of the ascetics, to enter into a tavern.

choices.why: The adjective is used substantivally for clergy in general; 'sacred persons' preserves the Greek sense of those set apart for sacred service without importing a later technical term.

choices.english: from presbyters as far as deacons
choices.why: The prepositional phrase marks the upper and lower bounds of the clerical range; 'as far as' renders ἕως literally and keeps the sense of a descending sequence.
The phrase refers to the ordered hierarchy of church offices; 'ecclesiastical rank' keeps the institutional sense of τάξις.
The term denotes a place where wine is sold and drunk; 'tavern' is the standard English equivalent and fits the disciplinary context.
The infinitive with δεῖ expresses the prohibition; 'to enter into' preserves the motion sense of the compound verb.

pass_b_english: No cleric, from presbyters as far as deacons and on through the ecclesiastical rank down to servants, readers, singers, exorcists, doorkeepers, or the order of ascetics, is to enter into a tavern.

problems.why: ἱερατικοὺς means 'clerics/priestly persons', not 'sacred person' which is too broad and vague.
problems.fix: No cleric, from presbyters down to deacons and through the ecclesiastical rank...
problems.ruling: ἱερατικοὺς means 'clerics/priestly persons'; 'sacred person' is too broad, changing the specific ecclesiastical reference.

fixed: Changed 'No sacred person' to 'No cleric' because ἱερατικοὺς means clerics or priestly persons, not sacred persons generally.

last_rejected.quote: from presbyters as far as deacons
last_rejected.why: Reverses hierarchy: source says 'from presbyters down to deacons', English implies presbyters are lower.
last_rejected.fix: from presbyters down to deacons, and on through the church rank down to servants
last_rejected.ruling: 'From X as far as Y' preserves source order; 'ἕως' denotes range endpoint, not downward direction. No hierarchy reversal occurs.
